question: Under Part 2 of the CPR, to which courts do the Civil Procedure Rules apply, and what exceptions exist for certain types of proceedings?
truth: Under Rule 2.1(1), the Civil Procedure Rules apply to all proceedings in (a) the County Court, (b) the High Court, and (c) the Civil Division of the Court of Appeal. Rule 2.1(2) provides that these Rules do not apply to proceedings of the kinds specified in the first column of a table (proceedings for which rules may be made under the enactments specified in the second column) except to the extent that they are applied to those proceedings by another enactment. [Part 2 – Application and Interpretation of the Rules]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What does Part 5 of the CPR provide regarding the preparation and supply of court documents, and when may a party prepare a document that would normally be prepared by the court?
truth: Part 5 contains general provisions about (a) documents used in court proceedings and (b) the obligations of a court officer in relation to those documents. Under Rule 5.2(1), where under the Rules a document is to be prepared by the court, the document may be prepared by the party whose document it is, unless (a) a court officer otherwise directs or (b) it is a document to which certain specified provisions apply. [Part 5 – Court Documents]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 6 of the CPR, what are the general rules about service of documents, and when does an alternative Part or practice direction take precedence over Part 6?
truth: Part 6 applies to the service of documents generally. Rule 6.1 provides that Part 6 applies to the service of documents, except where (a) another Part, any other enactment or a practice direction makes different provision, or (b) the court orders otherwise. The Part is divided into sections covering scope and interpretation, service within the jurisdiction, service out of the jurisdiction, and deemed dates of service. [Part 6 – Service of Documents]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 9 of the CPR, how may a defendant respond to particulars of claim, and what is the effect if particulars of claim have not yet been served?
truth: Part 9 sets out how a defendant may respond to particulars of claim. Under Rule 9.1(1), the Part establishes the available responses. Rule 9.1(2) provides that where the defendant receives a claim form which states that particulars of claim are to follow, he need not respond to the claim until the particulars of claim have been served on him. The defendant may respond by filing a defence, filing an admission, or filing an acknowledgment of service. [Part 9 – Responding to Particulars of Claim – General]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What are the requirements for filing an acknowledgment of service under Part 10 of the CPR, and in what circumstances must a defendant file one?
truth: Under Part 10, Rule 10.1(1) provides that the Part deals with the filing of an acknowledgment of service. Rule 10.1(2) states that where the claimant uses the procedure set out in Part 8 (alternative procedure for claims), Part 10 applies subject to the modifications set out in rule 8.3. Rule 10.1(3) provides that a defendant must file an acknowledgment of service if the defendant is unable to file a defence within the period specified, or the defendant wishes to dispute the court's jurisdiction. [Part 10 – Acknowledgement of Service]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 11 of the CPR, what is the procedure for a defendant who wishes to dispute the court's jurisdiction to try a claim?
truth: Under Rule 11(1), a defendant who wishes to (a) dispute the court's jurisdiction to try the claim, or (b) argue that the court should not exercise its jurisdiction, may apply to the court for an order declaring that it has no such jurisdiction or should not exercise any jurisdiction which it may have. The defendant must first file an acknowledgment of service under Part 10. [Part 11 – Disputing the Court's Jurisdiction]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What are the rules governing pre-action admissions under Part 14 of the CPR, and when may a pre-action admission be withdrawn?
truth: Under Rule 14.1(1), a person may, by notice in writing (a) admit the whole or any part of another party's case before commencement of proceedings (a 'pre-action admission'), and (b) withdraw a pre-action admission before commencement of proceedings, if the person to whom the admission was made agrees. Rule 14.1(2) provides that after commencement of proceedings, a pre-action admission may be withdrawn with the permission of the court. [Part 14 – Admissions]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 15 of the CPR, what must a defendant do if they wish to defend a claim, and what is the consequence of not filing a defence?
truth: Under Rule 15.2, a defendant who wishes to defend all or part of a claim must file a defence. Part 15 does not apply where the claimant uses the procedure set out in Part 8 (Rule 15.1). Part 14 contains further provisions which apply where the defendant admits a claim. If a defence is not filed, the claimant may obtain default judgment under Part 12. The defendant should also have regard to Rule 15.4 regarding the consequence of not filing a defence. [Part 15 – Defence and Reply]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 17 of the CPR, when may a party amend their statement of case without permission and when is the court's permission required?
truth: Under Rule 17.1(1), a party may amend their statement of case, including by removing, adding or substituting a party, at any time before it has been served on any other party. Rule 17.1(2) provides that if the statement of case has been served, a party may amend it only (a) with the written consent of all the other parties, or (b) with the permission of the court. This gives parties flexibility before service but requires agreement or court approval after service. [Part 17 – Amendments to Statements of Case]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What special provisions does Part 21 of the CPR contain for proceedings involving children and protected parties?
truth: Under Rule 21.1(1), Part 21 (a) contains special provisions which apply in proceedings involving children and protected parties, (b) sets out how a person becomes a litigation friend, and (c) sets out rules for the appointment and powers of litigation friends. A child or protected party must have a litigation friend to conduct proceedings on their behalf, except where the court makes an order permitting the child or protected party to conduct proceedings without a litigation friend. [Part 21 – Children and Protected Parties]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 25 of the CPR, what types of interim remedies are available, and list the specific orders the court may grant?
truth: Under Rule 25.1(1), interim remedies include (a) an interim injunction, (b) an interim declaration, (c) an order for the detention, custody or preservation of relevant property, (d) an order for the inspection of relevant property, (e) an order authorising a person to enter land or building for the purposes of carrying out an order, (f) an order for the delivery up of goods, (g) an order directing a party to provide information about the location of relevant property, (h) an order for the interim payment of a sum of money, and various other forms of interim relief. The Part also addresses security for costs in Section II. [Part 25 – Interim Remedies and Security for Costs]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Explain the scope and purpose of Part 27 of the CPR regarding the small claims track, including the limits on recoverable costs.
truth: Part 27 sets out the special procedure for dealing with claims which have been allocated to the small claims track under Part 26. Under Rule 27.1(1)(a), the Part sets out the special procedure for such claims, and under Rule 27.1(1)(b), it limits the amount of costs that can be recovered in respect of a claim allocated to the small claims track. Rule 27.14 deals with costs on the small claims track. The small claims track is designed to be accessible to litigants in person with simplified procedures and limited costs exposure. [Part 27 – The Small Claims Track]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What is the scope of Part 28 of the CPR regarding the fast track and intermediate track, and how does it relate to Parts 27 and 29?
truth: Part 28 contains general provisions about the management of cases allocated to the fast and intermediate tracks. Rule 28.1 provides that the Part's general provisions apply to both tracks. Section II contains further provisions about the fast track, while Section III addresses the intermediate track. Part 27 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the small claims track, and Part 29 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the multi-track. Together, Parts 26-29 form the complete track allocation and management framework. [Part 28 – The Fast Track and The Intermediate Track]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 29 of the CPR, what is the scope of the multi-track provisions and how does the court manage cases on this track?
truth: Under Rule 29.1, Part 29 contains general provisions about management of cases allocated to the multi-track and applies only to cases allocated to that track. Part 27 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the small claims track, and Part 28 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the fast track or intermediate track. On the multi-track, the court exercises active case management including setting timetables, giving directions, and conducting case management conferences. [Part 29 – The Multi-track]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 30 of the CPR, what types of transfers of proceedings does the Part deal with, and what supplementary provision does Practice Direction 30 make?
truth: Under Rule 30.1(1), Part 30 deals with the transfer of proceedings within the County Court, between the High Court and the county courts, and within the High Court. Rule 30.1(2) provides that Practice Direction 30 makes provision about the transfer of proceedings between courts. The Part establishes the framework for moving cases between different courts and levels of judiciary as appropriate. [Part 30 – Transfer]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 37 of the CPR, what are the provisions about payments into court, and what types of payments does this Part govern?
truth: Part 37 deals with miscellaneous provisions about payments into court. The Part covers situations where money may or must be paid into court, including where a defendant wishes to make a payment into court, where the court orders money to be paid into court, and the procedures for making and accepting payments. The Part works in conjunction with Practice Direction 37 which provides supplementary direction. [Part 37 – Miscellaneous Provisions About Payments Into Court]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 38 of the CPR, what is the procedure by which a claimant may discontinue all or part of a claim, and what costs consequences follow?
truth: Under Rule 38.1(1), the rules in Part 38 set out the procedure by which a claimant may discontinue all or part of a claim. A 'claim' includes a cause of action or part of one. Rule 38.1(2) provides that a claimant who (a) claims more than one remedy and (b) subsequently abandons their claim to one or more of the remedies but continues with their claim for the other remedies, is not treated as discontinuing a claim. A claimant who discontinues is generally liable for the costs of the proceedings unless the court otherwise orders. [Part 38 – Discontinuance]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 39 of the CPR, what are the general provisions relating to hearings, including the general rule about hearings being in public?
truth: Part 39 contains miscellaneous provisions relating to hearings. The general rule is that hearings are to be held in public. The court may order that a hearing or any part of it be held in private in certain specified circumstances. The Part also deals with failure of parties to attend hearings and the consequences thereof. [Part 39 – Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Hearings]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: What does Part 40 of the CPR provide regarding judgments and orders, including the standard requirements for every judgment or order?
truth: Part 40 sets out rules about judgments, orders, sale of land, etc. Section I addresses Judgments and Orders. Rule 40.1 provides that the section sets out rules about judgments and orders which apply except where any other of these Rules or a practice direction makes a different provision. Under Rule 40.2(1), every judgment or order must state the name and judicial title of the person who made it. The Part covers standard requirements, drawing up and filing of judgments and orders, consent orders, and sales of land. [Part 40 – Judgments, Orders, Sale of Land Etc.]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 41 of the CPR, what are the provisions regarding provisional damages and in what circumstances may a claimant claim them?
truth: Part 41 deals with damages, including provisional damages. Provisional damages may be awarded where the claimant has suffered personal injuries and there is a chance that at some definite or indefinite time in the future the claimant will develop some serious disease or suffer some serious deterioration in their physical or mental condition as a result of the act or omission which gave rise to the cause of action. The Part works alongside Practice Direction 41A (Provisional Damages) and Practice Direction 41B (Periodical Payments). [Part 41 – Damages]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 42 of the CPR, what are the provisions regarding change of solicitor, including the duties when a solicitor ceases to act?
truth: Part 42 deals with change of solicitor. The Part sets out the procedure to be followed when a party changes their solicitor or when a solicitor ceases to act. The party's former solicitor and new solicitor must comply with the specified notification and filing requirements. Practice Direction 42 supplements the Part with further procedural detail. [Part 42 – Change of Solicitor]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 45 of the CPR, explain the scope of fixed costs provisions and the types of proceedings to which fixed costs apply.
truth: Part 45 deals with fixed costs. The Part establishes fixed amounts of costs that are recoverable between parties in various types of proceedings. It contains multiple sections covering costs on commencement, costs on entry of judgment, costs on allocation and re-allocation, and specific provisions for different claim types including road traffic accident claims, personal injury claims, and other specified proceedings. Practice Direction 45 provides the detailed tables of fixed costs. [Part 45 – Fixed Costs]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 47 of the CPR, what is the procedure for detailed assessment of costs and what are the default provisions when costs are payable?
truth: Part 47 deals with the procedure for assessment of costs and default provisions. The Part sets out how detailed assessment proceedings are commenced, conducted, and concluded. It provides the procedure for requesting a detailed assessment hearing, the right to file points of dispute and replies, and the default provisions that apply when the paying party fails to commence detailed assessment proceedings. Practice Direction 47 supplements the Part with detailed procedural requirements. [Part 47 – Procedure for Assessment of Costs and Default Provisions]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 54 of the CPR, what is the scope of judicial review, and what types of decisions may be challenged through the judicial review procedure?
truth: Under Rule 54.1(1), Section I of Part 54 contains rules about judicial review. Rule 54.1(2) defines a 'claim for judicial review' as a claim to review the lawfulness of (i) an enactment, or (ii) a decision, action or failure to act in relation to the exercise of a public function. The claim must be filed promptly and in any event not later than 3 months after the grounds to make the claim first arose (Rule 54.5). Permission is required to proceed with judicial review. The Administrative Court has jurisdiction over judicial review claims. [Part 54 – Judicial Review and Statutory Review]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 55 of the CPR, what types of possession claims are covered, and what special provisions exist for coronavirus-related cases?
truth: Part 55 deals with possession claims. Rule 55.A1 provides that Practice Direction 55C makes provision for how claims under the Part (including appeals) are to proceed following the expiry of the stay provided for by rule 55.29. The Part covers claims for possession of land, including residential and commercial premises. It has effect subject to Practice Direction 55C for the period specified. The Part addresses both standard possession claims and accelerated procedures. [Part 55 – Possession Claims]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 57 of the CPR, what types of proceedings does the Part cover, and what are the main areas of probate, inheritance and presumption of death?
truth: Part 57 deals with probate, inheritance, presumption of death and guardianship of missing persons. The Part provides rules for proceedings relating to the validity of wills (probate claims), claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975, applications for presumption of death orders, and guardianship of missing persons. Practice Direction 57 supplements the Part with detailed procedural requirements. [Part 57 – Probate, Inheritance, Presumption of Death and Guardianship of Missing Persons]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 64 of the CPR, what types of proceedings relating to estates, trusts and charities does the Part govern?
truth: Part 64 deals with proceedings relating to estates, trusts and charities. The Part provides rules for claims and applications in relation to the administration of estates of deceased persons, the execution of trusts, and charity proceedings. Practice Direction 64A (Estates, Trusts and Charities) and Practice Direction 64B (Applications to the Court for directions by trustees) supplement the Part. [Part 64 – Estates, Trusts and Charities]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 66 of the CPR, what are the special rules that apply to Crown proceedings and how do they modify the general procedure?
truth: Part 66 deals with Crown proceedings. The Part sets out special rules that apply to proceedings by or against the Crown. The Crown may be subject to certain modified procedures in relation to service, judgment, and enforcement. Practice Direction 66 supplements the Part. The Part interacts with the Crown Proceedings Act 1947 and makes specific provisions regarding the manner in which the Crown may be sued and how proceedings are conducted. [Part 66 – Crown Proceedings]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 67 of the CPR, what types of proceedings relating to solicitors are covered?
truth: Part 67 deals with proceedings relating to solicitors. The Part provides rules for specific types of proceedings involving solicitors, including applications for orders relating to solicitors under the Solicitors Act 1974 and other relevant legislation. Practice Direction 67 provides supplementary procedural requirements. [Part 67 – Proceedings Relating to Solicitors]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 68 of the CPR, what proceedings does the Part govern in relation to the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018?
truth: Part 68 deals with proceedings under the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. The Part provides specific procedural rules for claims and applications arising under the EU Withdrawal Act, including retained EU law challenges and related proceedings in the High Court and Court of Appeal. [Part 68 – Proceedings under the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 69 of the CPR, what is the court's power to appoint a receiver, and what conditions must be met before a receiver may be appointed?
truth: Part 69 deals with the court's power to appoint a receiver. The Part sets out the circumstances in which the court may appoint a receiver, the procedure for applying for the appointment of a receiver, and the powers and duties of an appointed receiver. Practice Direction 69 sets out the prerequisites, including that before proceedings are started, certain conditions must be satisfied. [Part 69 – Court's Power to Appoint a Receiver]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 70 of the CPR, what are the general rules about enforcement of judgments and orders, and which other Parts contain rules about specific methods of enforcement?
truth: Under Rule 70.1(1), Part 70 contains general rules about enforcement of judgments and orders. Rule 70.1 notes that rules about specific methods of enforcement are contained in Parts 71 to 73, 81, 83, 84 and 89, and Schedule 2 CCR Order 28. The Part establishes the general framework within which the specific enforcement methods operate. A judgment creditor must typically apply for an enforcement method appropriate to the type of judgment and circumstances of the debtor. [Part 70 – General Rules about Enforcement of Judgments and Orders]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Part 72 of the CPR, explain the procedure for obtaining a third party debt order, including what a third party debt order achieves and the meaning of 'bank or building society'.
truth: Under Rule 72.1(1), Part 72 contains rules which provide for a judgment creditor to obtain an order for the payment to him of money which a third party who is within the jurisdiction owes to the judgment debtor. Rule 72.1(2) defines 'bank or building society' as including any person carrying on a business in the course of which he lawfully accepts deposits in the United Kingdom. The procedure involves an initial interim third party debt order followed by a hearing to consider making the order final. [Part 72 – Third Party Debt Orders]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: According to the Chancery Guide 2022, what is the scope and purpose of the Chancery Division, and what types of claims does it typically handle?
truth: The Chancery Guide (published July 2022, with updates in October 2022, June 2023, June 2024, and December 2024) sets out the practice and procedure of the Chancery Division of the High Court. The Chancery Division typically handles property disputes, trust litigation, estate administration, intellectual property matters, company law, insolvency, partnership disputes, and probate claims. The Guide supplements the CPR and its Practice Directions with specific guidance for Chancery practitioners. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: In the Chancery Division, what are the procedures for issuing claims and the key case management principles that govern proceedings?
truth: The Chancery Guide sets out case management principles for the Chancery Division including active judicial case management, proportionality, and cooperation between parties. Claims are issued through the standard CPR Part 7 or Part 8 procedure as appropriate. The Division emphasizes early identification of issues, realistic timetabling, and the use of alternative dispute resolution where appropriate. The guide covers pre-trial procedures, disclosure requirements, witness statements, expert evidence, and trial preparation specific to Chancery proceedings. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: What are the Chancery Division's requirements regarding disclosure and inspection of documents, and how do these differ from the standard CPR provisions?
truth: The Chancery Guide addresses disclosure and inspection in the context of the Business and Property Courts framework. For claims in the Chancery Division that fall within the Business and Property Courts, Practice Direction 57AD on disclosure applies. This provides for Extended Disclosure with specific Models (A through E) that go beyond standard disclosure under CPR Part 31. The Chancery Guide provides guidance on cost-effective disclosure and the use of technology in managing document review. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: In the Chancery Division, what are the procedures for applications, including without notice applications and urgent applications?
truth: The Chancery Guide provides detailed guidance on applications in the Chancery Division. Applications should generally be made on notice. Without notice (ex parte) applications are permitted in cases of urgency or where giving notice would defeat the purpose of the application. Urgent applications can be made outside normal court hours through the duty Chancery judge. The Guide specifies requirements for skeleton arguments, evidence, bundles, and time estimates for different types of application. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: What guidance does the Chancery Guide provide regarding trial preparation, skeleton arguments, and trial bundles in the Chancery Division?
truth: The Chancery Guide sets out requirements for trial preparation including preparation of trial bundles, filing of skeleton arguments, and provision of trial timetables. Skeleton arguments must be filed within specified time limits before trial. Trial bundles must be paginated, indexed, and contain only necessary documents. The Guide provides specific requirements for reading lists, chronologies, and lists of issues. The parties should agree trial timetabling and the use of technology for presentation of evidence where appropriate. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: Explain the purpose and scope of the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims, and to which track of claims does it primarily apply?
truth: The Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims is primarily designed for personal injury claims which are likely to be allocated to the fast track and to the entirety of those claims, not only to the personal injury element of a claim which also includes, for instance, property damage. Under paragraph 1.1.1, the Protocol sets out the steps the parties should follow before commencing proceedings. It encourages early exchange of information, early investigation, and the use of alternative dispute resolution to settle claims without litigation where possible. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under the Pre-Action Protocol for Construction and Engineering Disputes, what is the scope of the protocol and what types of claims does it apply to?
truth: Under paragraph 1.1, the Pre-Action Protocol for Construction and Engineering Disputes (2nd edition) applies to all construction and engineering disputes, including professional negligence claims against architects, engineers and quantity surveyors. Under paragraph 2.1, a claimant shall not be required to comply with the Protocol before commencing proceedings to the extent that the proposed proceedings require urgency or limitation periods are about to expire. The Protocol encourages early exchange of information and negotiation. [Pre-Action Protocol for Construction and Engineering Disputes]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under the Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review, what steps must a claimant take before commencing judicial review proceedings, and what is the relationship between the protocol and the time limit under Rule 54.5?
truth: The Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review applies to proceedings within England and Wales only. Under paragraph 1, it does not affect the time limit specified by Rule 54.5(1) of the CPR, which requires that any claim form in an application for judicial review must be filed promptly and in any event not later than 3 months after the grounds to make the claim first arose. The claimant should send a letter before claim to the defendant, setting out the issues in dispute and allowing a reasonable time for the defendant to respond before commencing proceedings. [Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 2A, what are the provisions regarding court offices and their functions in relation to proceedings?
truth: Practice Direction 2A supplements Part 2 of the CPR and provides information about court offices, their locations and functions. It assists litigants in identifying the correct court office for filing and managing proceedings. The Practice Direction sets out which types of business are handled by different court offices and provides supplementary guidance on the application of the Rules. [Practice Direction 2A – Court Offices]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 3A, what are the grounds on which the court may strike out a statement of case?
truth: Practice Direction 3A supplements CPR Part 3 regarding striking out a statement of case. The court may strike out a statement of case under Rule 3.4(2) on the grounds that (a) the statement of case discloses no reasonable grounds for bringing or defending the claim, (b) the statement of case is an abuse of the court's process or is otherwise likely to obstruct the just disposal of the proceedings, or (c) there has been a failure to comply with a rule, practice direction or court order. The Practice Direction provides guidance on the procedure for strike out applications. [Practice Direction 3A – Striking Out a Statement of Case]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 6A, what are the methods of service within the United Kingdom, and what are the deemed dates of service for each method?
truth: Practice Direction 6A supplements Part 6 of the CPR and provides detailed guidance on service within the United Kingdom. It covers the methods of service available, including personal service, first class post, leaving at a specified place, document exchange, fax, and other electronic means. The Practice Direction specifies deemed dates of service for each method, addresses service on particular types of parties (individuals, companies, partnerships), and provides guidance on service at the correct address. [Practice Direction 6A – Service Within the United Kingdom]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 22, what are the requirements for statements of truth, who must sign them, and what are the consequences of a false statement?
truth: Practice Direction 22 supplements Part 22 of the CPR regarding statements of truth. A statement of truth verifies that the facts stated in the document are true. It must be signed by the party or their legal representative. The person signing must believe the facts stated are true. Proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against a person who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth. The Practice Direction specifies the form of the statement of truth for different types of document. [Practice Direction 22 – Statements of Truth]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 40B, what are the rules regarding judgments and orders, including the standard form requirements and the procedure for drawing up orders?
truth: Practice Direction 40B supplements Part 40 of the CPR and deals with judgments and orders. It provides guidance on standard requirements including that every judgment or order must state the name and judicial title of the judge who made it. The Practice Direction covers the drawing up of orders, the sealing of orders by the court, consent orders, and Tomlin orders. It also deals with corrections to judgments and orders under the slip rule. [Practice Direction 40B – Judgments and Orders]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 52A, what are the general provisions about appeals and how does the appeals framework operate across different courts?
truth: Practice Direction 52A supplements Part 52 of the CPR regarding appeals. It sets out the general provisions about appeals including routes of appeal, permission to appeal requirements, and administrative procedures. Appeals from district judges generally go to circuit judges, from circuit judges to High Court judges, and from High Court judges to the Court of Appeal. The Practice Direction specifies the documentation required, time limits, and procedural steps for commencing and pursuing appeals. [Practice Direction 52A – Appeals]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 54A, what are the detailed procedures for judicial review claims, including the stages of the permission application?
truth: Practice Direction 54A supplements Part 54 of the CPR regarding judicial review. It sets out the detailed procedures for judicial review claims including the pre-action protocol stage, filing of the claim form, the permission stage, and the substantive hearing. The claimant must file a claim form in the Administrative Court and the court will consider whether to grant permission to proceed on the papers initially. If permission is refused on paper, the claimant may request an oral hearing. The Practice Direction covers case management, skeleton arguments, and the conduct of hearings. [Practice Direction 54A – Judicial Review]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 55A, what are the procedures for possession claims, including the requirements for different types of possession proceedings?
truth: Practice Direction 55A supplements Part 55 of the CPR regarding possession claims. It covers claims for possession of land by landlords, mortgagees, and others. The Practice Direction specifies the forms to be used, the evidence required, and the procedures for different types of possession claims including those based on rent arrears, anti-social behaviour, and trespass. It requires defendants to be given adequate notice and specifies the hearing procedure. [Practice Direction 55A – Possession Claims]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 57AD, what are the disclosure models available in the Business and Property Courts, and how does Extended Disclosure work?
truth: Practice Direction 57AD provides for disclosure in the Business and Property Courts, replacing standard disclosure under Part 31 for cases in those courts. It introduces five disclosure models: Model A (no order for disclosure), Model B (limited disclosure), Model C (request-led search-based disclosure), Model D (narrow search-based disclosure, with or without narrative documents), and Model E (wide search-based disclosure). Parties must complete a Disclosure Review Document identifying the issues for disclosure and the appropriate model for each issue. The Practice Direction requires parties to act reasonably and proportionately. [Practice Direction 57AD – Disclosure in the Business and Property Courts]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 1A, what provisions exist for the participation of vulnerable parties or witnesses in civil proceedings?
truth: Practice Direction 1A addresses the participation of vulnerable parties or witnesses in proceedings. The court should ensure that vulnerable parties and witnesses can give their best evidence and participate effectively. The Practice Direction provides for 'ground rules hearings' to identify measures that should be put in place, which may include the use of intermediaries, screens, live links, or break times. The court must take into account the needs of the person and the views of the person and their representative. [Practice Direction 1A – Participation of Vulnerable Parties or Witnesses]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: In the Commercial Court, what is the procedure for commencing proceedings under Section B of the Commercial Court Guide, and how does it differ from standard CPR procedures?
truth: Under Section B of the Commercial Court Guide (11th Edition, July 2023), claims in the Commercial Court should be started by issuing a Part 7 claim form or, in appropriate cases, a Part 8 claim form. The claim form must be marked 'Queen's Bench Division, Commercial Court' (now King's Bench Division). The Commercial Court Guide provides additional requirements beyond the standard CPR provisions, including requirements for case management information sheets and early identification of issues. The court requires parties to cooperate and to follow the disclosure regime under Practice Direction 57AD. [Commercial Court Guide]
category: Commercial Court

question: In the Technology and Construction Court, according to Section 1.1, how is the TCC defined and what types of disputes does it handle?
truth: According to Section 1.1 of the Technology and Construction Court Guide (October 2022), the TCC is a specialist court that forms part of the Business and Property Courts of England and Wales. The TCC handles claims which involve technically complex issues or questions, including building, engineering, and construction disputes, claims by or against local authorities relating to their statutory duties concerning land or buildings, claims relating to the design, supply and installation of mechanical and electrical systems, claims relating to the quality of goods or materials, and IT disputes. [Technology and Construction Court Guide]
category: Technology and Construction Court

question: In the Patents Court, to which track are actions allocated, and what are the requirements for case management?
truth: According to the Patents Court Guide (February 2025), actions in the Patents Court are allocated to the multi-track. The Guide references CPR Part 63 and the relevant Practice Directions for intellectual property claims. Case management in the Patents Court includes requirements for case management conferences, disclosure, experiments, and expert evidence specific to patent litigation. The court will give directions tailored to the complexity and nature of the patent dispute. [Patents Court Guide]
category: Patents Court

question: In the King's Bench Division, according to the 2025 Guide, what are the provisions regarding litigation friends and protected parties under CPR Part 21?
truth: The King's Bench Division Guide (2025 Edition) addresses the provisions of CPR Part 21 regarding children and protected parties. Where a child or protected party is involved in proceedings, a litigation friend must be appointed to conduct the proceedings on their behalf. The Guide provides practical guidance on how these provisions are applied within the King's Bench Division, including requirements for approval of settlements involving children or protected parties, and the role of the Official Solicitor. [King's Bench Division Guide]
category: King's Bench Division

question: What cross-referencing exists between CPR Part 3 case management powers and the different Court Guides? How do the Commercial Court, TCC, and Chancery Division each apply Part 3?
truth: CPR Part 3 grants the court general case management powers including the power to extend or shorten time, adjourn or bring forward hearings, require attendance, stay proceedings, consolidate proceedings, and strike out statements of case. The Commercial Court Guide applies Part 3 within its own framework under Section D (Case Management), requiring Case Management Conferences and pre-trial reviews. The TCC Guide applies Part 3 through Section 8 (Preliminary Issues) with emphasis on construction-specific case management. The Chancery Guide applies Part 3 through its own case management provisions adapted for property, trust and estate matters. Each court may exercise Part 3 powers in a manner suited to its specialist jurisdiction. [Part 3 – The Court's Case Management Powers] [Commercial Court Guide] [Technology and Construction Court Guide] [Chancery Guide]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: How do the rules on costs under CPR Part 44 interact with the specific costs provisions in the Commercial Court Guide and the Technology and Construction Court Guide?
truth: CPR Part 44 contains general rules about costs including the court's discretion, factors to consider in deciding costs, and the basis of assessment. The Commercial Court Guide (Section I: Costs) provides additional guidance specific to commercial litigation, including requirements for costs budgeting and summary assessment in shorter trials. The TCC Guide (Section 16: Costs) addresses summary assessment of costs in TCC proceedings, with particular attention to construction dispute costs. Both Court Guides operate within the framework of Part 44 but provide specialist guidance on costs management and budgeting proportionate to the claims heard in their respective courts. [Part 44 – General Rules About Costs] [Commercial Court Guide] [Technology and Construction Court Guide]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: How does CPR Part 52 on appeals interact with the appellate provisions in the Patents Court Guide for appeals to the Court of Appeal?
truth: CPR Part 52 contains the general rules about appeals. The Patents Court Guide (Section 21 and Annex G) provides specific guidance for appeals from the Patents Court to the Court of Appeal. Under Part 52, permission to appeal is required and may be granted by the lower court or the appeal court. The Patents Court Guide sets out the procedure for obtaining permission, preparing appeal bundles, and the specialized requirements for patent appeals including the presentation of technical evidence on appeal. Annex G specifically covers the procedure in IP appeals to the Court of Appeal. [Part 52 – Appeals] [Patents Court Guide]
category: Patents Court

question: Compare the disclosure requirements across the Commercial Court, Chancery Division, and TCC. How does Practice Direction 57AD apply differently in each?
truth: Practice Direction 57AD applies to all Business and Property Courts including the Commercial Court, Chancery Division, and TCC. However, each court's Guide provides specific supplementary guidance. The Commercial Court Guide (Appendix 15) provides guidance on disclosure where PD 57AD does not apply, and on the selection of disclosure models. The Chancery Guide addresses Extended Disclosure with particular reference to trust, property and estate proceedings where documentary evidence is often extensive. The TCC Guide (Sections on disclosure) addresses disclosure specific to construction disputes, including disclosure of technical documents, drawings and expert reports. All three courts use the five disclosure models (A through E) from PD 57AD. [Practice Direction 57AD] [Commercial Court Guide] [Chancery Guide] [Technology and Construction Court Guide]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: How do the witness statement requirements differ between the TCC Guide and the Patents Court Guide?
truth: The TCC Guide (Section 12) addresses witness statements with particular emphasis on construction disputes, requiring statements to deal with technical and factual issues clearly and to avoid argument. Section 12.2.2 addresses reluctant witnesses and the procedural steps a party must take. The Patents Court Guide provides specific guidance on witness statements in patent litigation, including statements dealing with technical matters and prior art. Both guides operate within the CPR Part 32 framework but adapt the requirements to their specialist jurisdictions. Evidence in patent cases often involves technical experts and industry witnesses, while TCC cases frequently involve site witnesses and project managers. [Technology and Construction Court Guide] [Patents Court Guide]
category: Technology and Construction Court

question: Under Practice Direction 31B, what are the requirements for disclosure of electronic documents, and what is the duty regarding preservation of documents?
truth: Practice Direction 31B addresses the disclosure of electronic documents. It imposes a duty to preserve documents that may be relevant to the issues in a case, including electronic documents and metadata. The parties should discuss the scope and extent of electronic disclosure at an early stage. The Practice Direction requires parties to consider the format in which electronic documents are to be disclosed, the use of keyword searches, and cost-effective approaches to managing electronic disclosure. A party's duty to preserve documents extends to electronic documents stored on servers, backup systems, portable devices, and cloud storage. [Practice Direction 31B – Disclosure of Electronic Documents]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 29, what are the provisions for management of cases allocated to the multi-track, and what directions will the court typically give?
truth: Practice Direction 29 supplements Part 29 of the CPR regarding the multi-track. It sets out the typical directions the court will give for cases allocated to the multi-track, including directions for disclosure, exchange of witness statements, exchange of expert reports, and preparation for trial. The court will typically give standard directions at the allocation stage and may hold case management conferences. The Practice Direction addresses the filing of listing questionnaires, the setting of trial windows, and the requirement for parties to cooperate in case management. [Practice Direction 29 – The Multi-Track]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 46, what are the provisions for costs in special cases, including the types of proceedings that attract special costs rules?
truth: Practice Direction 46 supplements Part 46 of the CPR regarding costs in special cases. It covers costs provisions for specific types of proceedings and parties, including costs relating to trustees and personal representatives, costs orders in favour of or against non-parties, and costs in group litigation. The Practice Direction also addresses wasted costs orders against legal representatives and costs in proceedings involving pro bono representation. [Practice Direction 46 – Costs Special Cases]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 7A, what are the requirements for starting proceedings using a claim form, and how does the production centre operate?
truth: Practice Direction 7A supplements Part 7 of the CPR and provides guidance on how to start proceedings using a claim form. It specifies the information that must be included in the claim form, the particulars of claim, and the address for service. The Practice Direction also covers the production centre and the issue of claim forms. Practice Direction 7B deals with the Production Centre specifically, and Practice Direction 7C addresses Money Claim Online. [Practice Direction 7A – How to Start Proceedings – The Claim Form]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: In the Circuit Commercial Court, according to B.2, what is the procedure for starting a case, and how does it differ from the main Commercial Court procedure?
truth: Under B.2 of the Circuit Commercial Court Guide (August 2023), a claimant issues proceedings in a Circuit Commercial Court by issuing a Part 7 or Part 8 claim form. The Circuit Commercial Courts are established in regional centres and handle commercial disputes of lesser complexity or value than those in the main Commercial Court. The procedure follows the CPR with modifications set out in Part 59 and Practice Direction 59. Unlike the main Commercial Court, the Circuit Commercial Court operates in regional venues and case management may differ, with certain provisions of the main Commercial Court Guide not applying (e.g., the pre-trial review process under D.7 may not be applied). [Circuit Commercial Court Guide]
category: Circuit Commercial Court

question: In the Chancery Division, what are the provisions regarding costs budgeting and costs management, and how does Practice Direction 3D apply?
truth: The Chancery Guide addresses costs management in the context of the Business and Property Courts. Practice Direction 3D on Costs Management requires parties in multi-track cases (where the amount claimed is less than £10 million) to file and exchange costs budgets. The court will then make a costs management order recording the extent to which budgets are agreed and approving or revising budgets. The Chancery Guide provides specific guidance on how costs budgeting operates in Chancery proceedings, where cases involving trusts, estates and property may have distinctive cost profiles requiring careful budgeting. [Chancery Guide] [Practice Direction 3D – Costs Management]
category: Chancery Division

question: In the Chancery Division, what procedures apply involving the Insolvency and Companies Court?
truth: The Chancery Division encompasses the Insolvency and Companies Court, which handles winding-up petitions, bankruptcy proceedings, and company-related applications. The Chancery Guide provides guidance on the procedures specific to insolvency and company matters, which fall within the broader Business and Property Courts framework. These proceedings are governed by the Insolvency Rules alongside the CPR, and the Chancery Guide provides practical directions for practitioners appearing in this specialist court. [Chancery Guide]
category: Chancery Division

question: Under Practice Direction 49E, what is the alternative procedure for claims, and what types of claims does it cover?
truth: Practice Direction 49E supplements the alternative procedure for claims and covers specific types of specialist proceedings. It provides a modified procedure for claims that do not require extensive factual investigation, including various types of statutory applications. The Practice Direction specifies which types of claims may use the alternative Part 8 procedure and what evidence is required. [Practice Direction 49E – Alternative Procedure for Claims]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 55B, what is the Possession Claims Online service and how does it operate?
truth: Practice Direction 55B provides for Possession Claims Online, which allows landlords and mortgage lenders to commence certain possession claims electronically. The service allows claims to be issued and managed online. The Practice Direction specifies which types of possession claims may use the online service, the requirements for filing and serving documents electronically, and the procedures for hearings. [Practice Direction 55B – Possession Claims Online]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Practice Direction 5A, what are the requirements regarding court documents, including the format and content requirements for documents filed at court?
truth: Practice Direction 5A supplements Part 5 of the CPR and provides detailed requirements for court documents. It specifies the format requirements for documents filed at court, including paper size, font size, margins, and pagination. The Practice Direction addresses the contents that must be included in various types of court document, the obligations of court officers, and the procedures for supplying documents from court records. [Practice Direction 5A – Court Documents]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

question: Under Policy Direction 27B, what is the claims procedure for personal injury claims below the small claims limit in road traffic accidents?
truth: Practice Direction 27B sets out the procedure for claims under the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims Below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents. It provides for a portal-based claims process designed to facilitate quick settlement of low-value RTA personal injury claims. The Practice Direction covers the stages of the claims process, time limits, and the fixed costs recoverable. [Practice Direction 27B – Claims Under the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims Below the Small Claims Limit]
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions
